title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
layout_note: Four 12 x 12 text-by-image matrices in a row, each one step of the chunked loss: initial per-device batches on the diagonal, then the local positive/negative blocks, then blocks swapped across devices, then the final cross-device sum.
grouping: Rows (T1..T12) and columns (I1..I12) carry header strips tinted by device (pink Device 1, purple Device 2, blue Device 3); the block computed at each step is outlined by a thick border in that device's colour.
shapes_depth: Flat grids of square cells; cells marked with '+', '-' or a check glyph; the active block filled pale yellow, the diagonal positives pale green; no 3-D or shadows.
proposed_highlight: The only cells being computed at a step are filled bright yellow and boxed in the device colour, while finished cells fade to check marks; per-device loss bars under each matrix show the running share (33%, 66%, check).
lesson: To explain a distributed computation, repeat the same matrix once per step and colour rows, columns and loss bars by the device that owns them, so the reader tracks ownership by colour alone.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue ICCV 2023 (not verified in this session). The paper's only method diagram: it shows the chunked sigmoid-loss implementation, not the encoders.

arrangement.units: four matrix panels left to right, separated by whitespace only, one per step of the loss computation
arrangement.inputs_as: column headers I1..I12 (images) and row headers T1..T12 (texts) grouped by device
arrangement.losses_at: a 'loss' bar under each matrix (from the second on), split into one segment per device; the last one sums across devices
arrangement.shared: devices are drawn as coloured header strips repeated in every panel; the row-device order rotates between panels to show the swap

taxonomy.task: memory-efficient sigmoid image-text loss across devices
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = pairwise sigmoid (binary) loss over all image-text pairs, the paper's replacement for the softmax contrastive loss

insights.structure: Four copies of the same 12 x 12 text-by-image matrix stand in a row, one per computation step, each with device-coloured header strips on its top and left edges.
insights.data: Pairs are cells: '+' on the diagonal for positives, '-' for negatives, a check mark for cells already counted, and the cells being computed now filled yellow inside a device-coloured outline.
insights.emphasis: Only the current block is bright yellow with a thick coloured border while everything finished fades to pale cells, so each panel shows exactly what one device holds at that moment.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right; small coloured arrows drop from each matrix's columns into a per-device loss bar whose percentages (33%, 66%, check) track progress, ending in a 'Cross Device sum' arrow.
insights.avoid: Nothing in the panels names the steps (no step titles or numbers), so the reader needs the caption to know that the rotating row-device labels mean a cross-device swap.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
